title: fix: keep agent temporary files in owned scratch
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agent validation commands can leave large temporary trees in host `/tmp`, outside OpenClaw's 24-hour scratch cleanup. On hosts where `/tmp` is tmpfs, that consumes memory and swap until an operator intervenes.

## User Impact

Local agent commands now default `TMPDIR`, `TMP`, and `TEMP` to their workspace's `.openclaw/tmp`. Temporary validation output is disposable under the existing 24-hour rule, even when artifacts reference it. Live and queued agent work remains protected; durable outputs belong outside scratch. After those runs settle, a detached background service alone does not extend the 24-hour lifetime of unchanged workspace scratch. Services needing longer-lived files must place them outside scratch or explicitly select a temp root with their own cleanup.

## Why This Change Was Made

Connect core exec, local CLI execution, and native Codex shell/Code Mode environment preparation to the existing scratch owner. Codex obtains the path through its run-bound host capability and applies it through thread shell policy, preserving shared app-server reuse. Docker/Podman commands use scratch in their writable workspace mount. Read-only workspaces keep writable temporary files in the container-private `/tmp` tmpfs, owned and released by the container lifecycle.

The existing cleanup inventory now includes configured agent and local sandbox workspaces, including sandbox directories left after container retirement. Queued protection uses the production session selector, including attachment grants and immutable skill-library isolation. Sandbox scope resolution and active-command custody reuse their existing owners. No new TTL implementation, configuration option, schema, reference-protection index, or cache. Explicit CLI/command/container environment overrides remain supported. Remote execution keeps its own paths. Programs that explicitly choose `/tmp` can bypass the policy; arbitrary host temp entries are not swept by name. Deep workspace paths can exceed Unix-domain socket limits: those tools need a short workspace or an explicit short-temp override with their own cleanup. The existing test runner already owns that exception.

Related: #193677. The short-lived native socket-path workaround from #196509 remains intact.

## Evidence

A real core exec from a nested working directory creates its temporary file inside checkout scratch. The committed regression fails on base `f685aad5977d707e47ba402b3d072e482a6b091b` at that assertion and passes with this change. Native Codex engine tests cover fresh and cold-resumed shells, login/snapshot variations, and restrictive environment filters. Local CLI tests cover default routing and explicit overrides; the generated sandbox shell creates an actual temporary directory. Hosted review identified a read-only-workspace regression; two real-shell tests reproduced it for Docker and Podman, and all 40 backend tests pass after preserving container-private temp for that mode. Cleanup tests verify expiry, live/queued protection, and queued sandbox protection after its last container registry row retires. Attachment and skill-library isolation regressions fail before the correction; all 17 custody and five managed-custody tests pass afterward. A real Docker read-only bind-mount probe fails before the temp-path correction and succeeds afterward.

Synthetic btrfs workload: 62,000 scratch files / 1.181 GB, beside a physical 37.63 GB synthetic SQLite storage fixture with 5,000 session rows. Five serial A1/A2 pairs per variant (10 observations each), using the same unchanged TTL owner:

| Metric | Inherited temp | Workspace temp |
|---|---:|---:|
| Expired validation scratch reclaimed | 0 | 670.56 MB |
| Total reclaimed, including existing coverage cleanup | 38.10 MB | 708.66 MB |
| Owner wall median / p95 | 2.118 / 3.123 s | 41.630 / 54.049 s |
| Deliberate pacing | 1.5 s | 29.0 s |
| Process CPU median / p95, workers included | 0.559 / 1.616 s | 11.075 / 14.684 s |
| Main-thread CPU median / p95 | 12.475 / 27.676 ms | 171.015 / 265.320 ms |
| Separate sampled main-isolate allocation A1 / A2 | 1.257 / 0.757 MB | 2.325 / 1.936 MB |

Every run preserves fresh/live/outside files and reports zero cleanup errors. This is the added cost of reclaiming previously unowned scratch, not a speedup comparison or a production-stall reproduction. A/A wall variation reached 24% on the shared virtual disk. The SQLite file supplies storage shape; this filesystem benchmark does not query the agent schema or measure whole-Gateway latency. Worker/native allocations are excluded from the heap sample.

Reproduce with `node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/scratch-cleanup-measure.ts --root <new-btrfs-directory> --samples 5 --mode timing --agent-temp`; use `--samples 1 --mode allocation` for the separate allocation pair.

Focused tests, the full package build, targeted typechecks/lint, formatting, line-cap checks, and final `pnpm check:changed` at `8c3d312db0fa258486ab502ad7ad128a83ed8600` pass. An earlier expanded check exposed an inherited SDK surface-budget regression: exact base and candidate both have 3,908 exports / 2,250 callables against limits 3,894 / 2,243. The check passes at `422ff062032e6`; the first expansion at `5795128db2d0c` (#201073) fails at 3,896 / 2,244. This is a main regression, not a budget change in this PR. No standalone SDK export was added. Final snapshot Codex autoreview is clean through P2. Production delta: +197/-49 = +148 lines, required for the missing environment handoffs, run-bound host operation, and root/custody coverage; repeated Codex placement checks and duplicate sandbox active-use logic were consolidated.
